_comment: EXAMPLE · SQL Server destination / write modes. `tables` declares one WRITE SLOT per entry, fed by input_tables in the same order. if_table_exists is the one decision: "append" (default) inserts and the table grows across runs, "replace" truncates then inserts so the count stays put — and NEITHER is an upsert (no key matching, no merge). Both CREATE the table when it is missing, which is also the only moment column types are decided: writing into an existing table uses that table's types. transactional=True (default) makes a multi-table write all-or-nothing; False commits per table. A returned None skips the write and does NOT truncate, so 'no data this run' never destroys what is there. Five sinks: write_append, write_replace, write_two_tables, write_without_transaction (+ dest_cfg chunk size), write_nothing. RE-RUN to watch customers_append grow while customers_replace stays at three rows. One function per file under functions/mssql_dest_modes/. Run: `tdx-xp oneshot --suite examples/mssql_dest_modes --keep`.
